reviewer: pending_independent_review (independent of original author and cancellation_commit_fix author)

findings.issue: Cancellation could commit after the initial cancelled check and after balance settlement but before final transition; POST then returned succeeded/output while cancel receipt and durable order were cancelled.
findings.minimal_fix_verified: A shared short terminal_commit_lock serializes cancellation and local final checkpoint/settlement/transition, checks actual committed state, suppresses cancelled response bodies, and leaves remote I/O outside the lock. A completed commit legitimately makes later cancellation return succeeded.

confirmed_properties: Round/lifetime budget reasons remain distinct from user cancellation; rejected received usage is charged once and no late model message or tool dispatch is published in the targeted runtime checks.
Provider slots release in provider/bridge finally after the synchronous adapter exits; historical raw capacity observations remain occupied after consumer cancellation then become available.
Diagnostic missing history remains unknown/not_established; saved whitelisted status/method/original timezone-bearing timestamp is preserved without a fresh probe or arbitrary probe text.

Nested collection allows only synchronous ryn_get_system_diagnostics -> ryn_list_devices with empty arguments and read effect, preserves original arguments/context, rejects wrong tasks/other edges, and clears parent scope in finally.

Context review was limited to the exact 39-addition/16-deletion runtime.py diff against .codex-tmp/runtime-before-context-repair.py plus the new test file; the common preexisting compaction design was not treated as new code.

Every _complete stage checks encoded(messages)+encoded(specs) before token reservation/model dispatch. Summary admission now measures the actual outer serialized summary messages, including string escaping, instead of the smaller intermediate source.

Summary-only copies unwrap top-level tool result JSON dict/list and tool-call argument JSON, without recursively parsing business strings or mutating the encrypted transcript. Owner constraints, exact continuation references, write permission enforcement and stored mutation receipts remain intact.

A 12000-byte context fixture traversed a closed two-call search exchange, compaction, approval, one write and readback; the parallel read-only variant rejected a forged summary claim of write approval.
confirmed_limitations: Consumer return does not establish upstream compute/billing cancellation; absent vendor usage remains unknown.
Historical physical-host evidence used the prior wheel; the newly repaired terminal-commit code has local deterministic validation, not renewed physical-host or Windows installer acceptance.
HTTP/relay blocking I/O interruption, every streaming-delta callback race, and atomic cancellation of arbitrary external callbacks are outside this final-response review.
Matched query observations remain development-only, with reference answer overclaiming history; no formal comparison, heldout or full acceptance result is inferred.
The context bound is the existing runtime metric: UTF-8 JSON message projection plus tool specifications, not a tokenizer estimate or the entire vendor HTTP envelope.
Long exchanges that still exceed the bound after protocol unwrapping fail closed. Offline fixture success does not prove the previously failed F08 real-model task now succeeds.
